title_jp: {健太|けんた}の{引き継ぎ|ひきつぎ}メモ
context: Friday: {村井|むらい}さん hands back アルちゃん's phone, dried and working, and he finally replies to レン. The next thing on it is a photo of {健太|けんた}'s handover note: tomorrow {健太|けんた} will be busy preparing the showdown, so アルちゃん runs reception alone in the afternoon.
scene: Your phone works again. Next on it: a photo of {健太|けんた}'s handover note for tomorrow, when you run reception alone.

phrases.jp: {雪|ゆき}のせいで、バスが{遅れて|おくれて|to be late, delayed|4}いるそうです。
phrases.en: Apparently the bus is late because of the snow.
phrases.note: What you tell a waiting guest. Noun + のせいで: never drop the の.

phrases.jp: {平日|へいじつ|weekday|3}に{比べて|くらべて|to compare|4}、{週末|しゅうまつ}はずっと{忙しい|いそがしい}ですね。
phrases.en: Compared with weekdays, weekends are much busier.
phrases.note: Aに{比|くら}べて = compared with A. ずっと before an adjective = much more.

phrases.jp: {確認|かくにん|checking, confirmation|4}してから、{折り返し|おりかえし|calling back|3}お{電話|でんわ}します。
phrases.en: I'll check and call you back.
phrases.note: The reception classic when you don't know the answer yet.

phrases.jp: {寝坊|ねぼう|oversleeping|4}したせいで、{朝ご飯|あさごはん}{食べられなかった|たべられなかった}…。
phrases.en: I overslept, so I couldn't eat breakfast…
phrases.note: Blaming yourself works too. {寝坊|ねぼう}する = to oversleep.

phrases.jp: {昨日|きのう}より、{今日|きょう}の{方|ほう}が{慣れて|なれて|to get used to|4}きた{気|き}がする。
phrases.en: I feel more used to it today than yesterday.
phrases.note: AよりBの{方|ほう}が = B more than A. 〜{気|き}がする softens it: 'I feel like'.

dialogue_setting: A handwritten note taped to the reception desk at ゲストハウス{風|かぜ}, sent by {健太|けんた} as a photo on LINE.
text_title: {土曜日|どようび}の{受付|うけつけ}メモ（{健太|けんた}より）

dialogue.speaker: Hello
dialogue.jp: アルちゃんへ。{明日|あした}は{対決|たいけつ|showdown, face-off|3}の{準備|じゅんび}のせいで、{俺|おれ}は{午後|ごご}ずっと{台所|だいどころ}や。{受付|うけつけ|reception (desk)|4}、{頼んだ|たのんだ}で！
dialogue.en: To アルちゃん. Because of the showdown prep, I'm in the kitchen all afternoon tomorrow. Reception is yours!
dialogue.note: Kansai: や = だ, {頼|たの}んだで = {頼|たの}んだよ.

dialogue.speaker: Weekdays vs weekends
dialogue.jp: {平日|へいじつ|weekday|3}に{比べて|くらべて}、{週末|しゅうまつ}はチェックインが{倍|ばい|double, twice as many|3}くらい{多い|おおい}。{特に|とくに}3{時|じ}から5{時|じ}が{混む|こむ}で。
dialogue.en: Compared with weekdays, there are about twice as many check-ins at weekends. 3 to 5 is the busiest.

dialogue.speaker: Guests
dialogue.jp: {週末|しゅうまつ}は{家族連れ|かぞくづれ|families with children|3}も{多い|おおい}。{外国|がいこく}のお{客|きゃく}さんより、{質問|しつもん}が{細かい|こまかい|detailed; small|4}{気|き}がする。
dialogue.en: At weekends there are lots of families too. I feel their questions are more detailed than the foreign guests'.

dialogue.speaker: Last week
dialogue.jp: {先週|せんしゅう}は{俺|おれ}が{予約|よやく}の{確認|かくにん|checking, confirmation|4}を{忘れた|わすれた}せいで、{部屋|へや}が{一つ|ひとつ}{足りなく|たりなく}なった。ほんまにごめん…。
dialogue.en: Last week, because I forgot to check a booking, we ended up one room short. Really sorry…
dialogue.note: ほんまに = {本当|ほんとう}に (Kansai).

dialogue.speaker: Rule
dialogue.jp: チェックインの{時|とき}は{必ず|かならず}{名前|なまえ}と{泊数|はくすう|number of nights|2}を{確認|かくにん}。{到着|とうちゃく|arrival|3}が{遅れる|おくれる|to be late, delayed|4}{客|きゃく}には{電話|でんわ}してな。
dialogue.en: At check-in, always confirm the name and number of nights. Phone any guest whose arrival is running late.

dialogue.speaker: You vs me
dialogue.jp: {正直|しょうじき|honestly, to be honest|4}、{受付|うけつけ}は{俺|おれ}より{丁寧|ていねい}やし、{評判|ひょうばん|reputation|3}もええ。でもトルティーヤは{負けへん|まけへん|(Kansai) = 負けない|2}で！
dialogue.en: Honestly, you're more polite than me at reception, and the guests like you. But I won't lose at tortilla!
dialogue.note: やし = だし, ええ = いい, {負|ま}けへん = {負|ま}けない (Kansai).

dialogue.speaker: P.S.
dialogue.jp: P.S. スマホ、{直った|なおった|to be fixed|4}？{直ったら|なおったら}スタンプ{一個|いっこ}{送って|おくって}な。
dialogue.en: P.S. Is your phone fixed? If it is, send me a sticker.
dialogue.note: {送|おく}ってな = {送|おく}ってね (Kansai).

listening.intro: In the afternoon your phone rings for the first time since the puddle: a voicemail from {恵子|けいこ}さん.

lines.jp: アルちゃん、{恵子|けいこ}です。{明日|あした}のじゃがいも、{納屋|なや|shed, barn|2}から{出して|だして}、{玄関|げんかん|entrance hall|3}に{置いて|おいて}おいたよ。
lines.en: アルちゃん, it's {恵子|けいこ}. I took tomorrow's potatoes out of the shed and left them in the entrance.

lines.jp: {卵|たまご}は{健太|けんた}くんが{買う|かう}んでしょう？{忘れないで|わすれないで}ね。
lines.en: {健太|けんた} is buying the eggs, right? Don't forget them.

listening.question: じゃがいもは{今|いま}どこにありますか。
listening.explain: {納屋|なや}から{出して|だして}、{玄関|げんかん}に{置いて|おいて}おいた: she took them out of the shed and left them in the entrance.

grammar.form: noun: + の + せいで ({雪|ゆき}のせいで, {準備|じゅんび}のせいで) · verb: plain form + せいで ({忘|わす}れたせいで, {寝坊|ねぼう}したせいで) · い-adj: + せいで ({寒|さむ}いせいで) · な-adj: + な + せいで ({下手|へた}なせいで)
grammar.explanation: Names the cause of a bad result, with a hint of blame: 'it's X's fault that…'. For good results use おかげで ('thanks to'). The classic mistake is dropping の after a noun: {雪|ゆき}のせいで, never {雪|ゆき}せいで. {私|わたし}のせいで = it's my fault.

examples.jp: {風邪|かぜ}のせいで、{声|こえ}が{出ない|でない}。
examples.en: I've lost my voice because of this cold.

examples.jp: {部屋|へや}が{寒い|さむい}せいで、{全然|ぜんぜん}{眠れなかった|ねむれなかった}。
examples.en: The room was so cold I couldn't sleep at all.

examples.jp: {私|わたし}のせいで{遅れて|おくれて|to be late|4}しまって、すみません。
examples.en: I'm sorry we're late because of me.

quiz.question: {台風|たいふう|typhoon|3}＿＿、{電車|でんしゃ}が{止まった|とまった}。
quiz.en: The trains stopped because of the typhoon.
quiz.explain: 台風 is a noun, so it needs の before せいで; おかげで is for good results.

quiz_more.question: {先生|せんせい}が{丁寧|ていねい}に{教えて|おしえて}くれた＿＿、{合格|ごうかく|passing (an exam)|3}できた。
quiz_more.en: Thanks to the teacher explaining carefully, I passed.
quiz_more.explain: A good result takes おかげで, and after a verb there's no の.

quiz_more.question: {説明|せつめい}が{下手|へた|bad at|4}＿＿、お{客|きゃく}さんを{困らせて|こまらせて}しまった。
quiz_more.en: Because my explanation was bad, I confused the guest.
quiz_more.explain: 下手 is a な-adjective: it keeps な before せいで.

kanji.where: The sign {健太|けんた} hangs on the guesthouse door on busy weekends, and the red label on booking sites when no rooms are left.
kanji.breakdown: {満室|まんしつ}: 満 full + 室 room → 'rooms full'.
kanji.related: {満席|まんせき} = all seats taken; {空室|くうしつ} = vacancy.

tip.title: Never leave without a handover
tip.body: In Japanese workplaces, even a part-timer passes on what's pending before a day off: this is {引き継ぎ|ひきつぎ}. A short written note is the norm, and it usually ends with よろしくお{願い|ねが}いします or a friendly {頼んだ|たのんだ}よ. Leaving without one looks careless, however good your work was.

challenge.prompt: You send {健太|けんた} a sticker. He replies at once: 「おっ、{直った|なおった|to be fixed|4}んや！よかったな。」 Tell him yes, it's fixed, but because of the puddle the camera has gone a bit weird.

options.jp: うん、{直った|なおった}！でも{水|みず}たまりのせいで、カメラがちょっと{変|へん}になった。
options.why: Noun + のせいで for a bad result, casual style for a coworker friend.

options.jp: うん、{直った|なおった}！でも{水|みず}たまりせいで、カメラがちょっと{変|へん}になった。
options.why: After a noun you need の: {水|みず}たまりのせいで.

options.jp: うん、{直った|なおった}！でも{水|みず}たまりのおかげで、カメラがちょっと{変|へん}になった。
options.why: おかげで means 'thanks to': it only sounds sarcastic with a bad result.

options.jp: うん、{直った|なおった}！でも{水|みず}たまりなせいで、カメラがちょっと{変|へん}になった。
options.why: な is only for な-adjectives; {水|みず}たまり is a noun, so it takes の.

challenge.model_answer: うん、{直った|なおった|to be fixed|4}！でも{水|みず}たまりのせいで、カメラがちょっと{変|へん}になった。
challenge.explanation: {水|みず}たまりのせいで puts the blame on the puddle: a noun takes の before せいで. {変|へん}になった = 'went weird'. Plain form and うん fit a chat with {健太|けんた}, who writes in casual Kansai-ben.
challenge.hint: noun + の + せいで, casual

vocab.note: {対|たい} against + {決|けつ} decide. TV loves it: {料理|りょうり}{対決|たいけつ} = cooking battle.
{受|う}ける receive + {付|つ}ける attach. Signs at hotels, hospitals, offices.
{平|へい} ordinary + {日|じつ} day. Opposite: {週末|しゅうまつ}, {土日|どにち}.
{倍|ばい}になる = to double. 3{倍|ばい} = three times as much.
{細|こま}かい{人|ひと} = a fussy person. {細|こま}かいお{金|かね} = small change.
{確|かく} certain + {認|にん} recognise. {確認|かくにん}する: you'll hear it at every counter.
Trains, people, arrivals. {遅|おそ}い is the adjective 'slow, late'.
Sentence opener: {正直|しょうじき}、… = 'to be honest…'. Also {正直|しょうじき}な{人|ひと}.
{評判|ひょうばん}がいい / {悪|わる}い. {評判|ひょうばん}の{店|みせ} = a popular shop.
Things get {直|なお}る; illnesses get {治|なお}る. Same sound.

kanji_study.parts: 石 stone radical + 隺 a bird flying high → as solid as stone: certain, confirmed.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 硬 (hard): both have 石 on the left, but 確 has 隺, 硬 has 更.

kanji_study.parts: ⻌ road radical (moving) + 尸 and 羊 sheep → a sheep plodding down the road: slow, late.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 達 (reach): both sit on ⻌, but 遅 has 尸 over 羊, 達 has 土 over 羊.

extras.title: Reception lines in keigo
extras.title_jp: {受付|うけつけ}の{敬語|けいご}
extras.intro: What {健太|けんた} switches to the moment a guest walks in.

items.jp: ご{予約|よやく}のお{名前|なまえ}をお{願い|ねがい}します。
items.en: May I have the name on the booking?
items.note: The first line at every check-in.

items.jp: {少々|しょうしょう|a little (polite)|3}お{待ち|まち}ください。
items.note: {少々|しょうしょう} = polite ちょっと.

items.jp: {本日|ほんじつ|today (formal)|3}は{満室|まんしつ|fully booked|2}でございます。
items.note: {本日|ほんじつ} = formal {今日|きょう}.

extras.title: More ways to compare
extras.title_jp: {比べる|くらべる}{言い方|いいかた}
extras.intro: Three patterns that sit next to より and に{比|くら}べて.

items.jp: {大阪|おおさか}の{冬|ふゆ}は、ここほど{寒く|さむく}ない。
items.en: Winter in Osaka isn't as cold as here.
items.note: AほどBない = not as B as A.

items.jp: {平日|へいじつ|weekday|3}のほうが{断然|だんぜん|by far|3}{楽|らく}だよ。
items.note: {断然|だんぜん} = by far, decidedly; casual and strong.

items.jp: どっちも{同じ|おなじ}くらい{美味しい|おいしい}。
items.note: {同|おな}じくらい = about the same: the diplomatic answer at a food showdown.
